I fucking buggy mess still a year since launch. I do have the bare minimum specs so I I knew going in running this game would be interesting. Frequent stutters, but the most annoying issue I dealt with was when I first ran it the game kept crashing. I figured out that for whatever reason windows defender wouldn't allow bl4 to make save data. Adding the game to the defenders expention list and running as administrator were the solution. I did have fun playing through, but these issues make it to where I can't in good faith recommend this game to anyone unless buying on a generous discount.

Okay so I wanna preface this with, the game is awesome. However Do not get it on PC. Unfortunately do to optimization issues it is nearly unplayable on PC even if your setup meets and exceeds the requirements like mine. It feels like a stuttering mess and takes at least 10 minutes to boot up. On PS5, it is as smooth as butter so if you do plan on playing take this into consideration. The game itself has some of the best graphics and effects I've seen, and from what I've read the map is 3X the size of Skyrim and is all being loaded simultaneously for 4-player Co-op. Hence the optimization issues. Great Game, just not on PC.

Well done. You killed it. You killed the franchise.

I have tried a lot of shader compilation simulators, but Borderlands 4 is untouchable. You get to compile shaders when you first launch the game (but hey everyone does that), but what is awesome is that you get to compile again WHILE the game launches, but that's not all! If you are using proton (because WTF, Linux is a thing), you get to compile them again before you get to the game menu!

Forget the atrocious optimization, forget the necessary upscaling and frame gen, just for a playable framerate on anything but a 9800X3D and a RTX 5090, if you are looking for some sweet shader compilation, look no further than Borderlands 4 _|_

As a long-time Borderlands fan, it kills me to write this review. But Borderlands 4 is a real dissapointment. Between meaningless in-game money, easy and boring bosses, and the game trying to sell you DLCs, this Borderlands is a farcry from what the franchise once was. My friends and I have played all of the Borderlands games over the years, and this was the first one we didn't want to finish. We were all left wanting a better experience, and wondering what happened to this once great franchise.

TLDR; Really Dissapointing

I love the borderlands franchise. I really wanted to like this game but i wont lie, i am sure i'm close to finishing and have more cons than pros. I waited to get it until it was on sale since the CEO of the company said " if you were a true fan, you'd fine a way to make it happen" when the pricing was outrageous when it first came out, that put a bad taste in my mouth. But now putting almost 100 hours into the game, i just... its too much. there is too much going on, you have no feelings towards the characters, old and new. i HATE that its just one big map instead of going to different planets, there are too many glitches, i feel more frustrated playing than actually having fun. it doesn't have the spark anymore. The gameplay just isn't like it used to be. At this point i'm just ready to finish the game then uninstall it. These are just my personal opinions.

- Runs terribly even with top of the line hardware
- Story isn't great but not terrible either, better than 3 but worse than 2
- Gameplay feels worse than previous titles
- World feels empty
- Terrible balancing
- Changes to the prestige system and drops in relation too it destroy replayability

Final deathblow to this dying series, just go play BL2 again

details.text: Players who have logged the least time are far less positive, at 25%, than those with more hours, at 63%.
